key_facts.fact: docs.exa.ai returns a 307 redirect to https://exa.ai/docs; the docs say the OpenAPI spec at https://exa.ai/docs/exa-spec.yaml ('Exa Public API' v2.0.0) is the source of truth for request and response schemas.
Base URL is https://api.exa.ai; auth is 'x-api-key: KEY' or 'Authorization: Bearer KEY'; keys are created at https://dashboard.exa.ai/api-keys; both SDKs read EXA_API_KEY.
/search type enum is instant, fast, auto (default), deep-lite, deep, deep-reasoning; neural and keyword are not in the current API enum.
Documented latencies: instant ~250 ms, fast ~450 ms, auto ~1 s, deep-lite ~4 s, deep 4-15 s, deep-reasoning 12-40 s; outputSchema adds about 2 s.
The product page gives different latencies (Instant 323 ms, Fast 450 ms, Auto ~1.2 s, Deep 4-12 s) and a benchmark of Exa Deep 80.0% accuracy at 4.3 s versus Perplexity 50.0% and Brave 43.0%.
The /research endpoint was retired on April 1, 2026 and replaced by /search with type deep-reasoning; both SDKs still ship an exa.research client that calls /research/v1.
/findSimilar is deprecated (deprecated: true, Deprecation header); Exa says to use /search with a query describing the source.
Category values: company, publication, news, personal site, financial report, people. company and people reject startPublishedDate, endPublishedDate and excludeDomains with a 400.
numResults ranges from 1 to 100 (default 10), with no pagination; each result above 10 costs $1 per 1,000.

On /search, outputSchema returns output.content plus output.grounding[{field, citations[{url,title}], confidence low/medium/high}]. Object schemas are capped at 10 total properties and 2 nesting levels, and every array needs items.
Content options go inside 'contents' on /search but at the top level on /contents; /contents takes ids or urls (1-100), never both.
maxAgeHours replaces livecrawl: omitted = cache with fetch fallback, N = fetch if older than N hours, 0 = always fetch, -1 = cache only, max 720; livecrawlTimeout defaults to 10000 ms (max 90000).
Dynamic Highlights (highlights.dynamic) is a research preview that requires the header 'Exa-Beta: dynamic-highlights-2026-08-28' and cannot be combined with maxCharacters.
Pricing: instant $4/1k, fast and auto $7/1k, deep-lite and deep $12/1k, deep-reasoning $15/1k, contents $1/1k pages per content type, answer $5/1k, monitors $15/1k, summaries $1/1k pages.
Free tier: $10 in credits on signup, reset to $10 on the 1st of each month (non-accumulating), plus a one-time $10 onboarding bonus; no payment method required.

Default rate limits: /search, /answer and /chat/completions 10 QPS; deep types 5 QPS; /contents 100 QPS; /agent/runs and /responses 5 QPS with 50 active runs; /websets 20 QPS. Buying $1,000 of credits in 30 days unlocks 25 QPS for 90 days.

Agent effort values are minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, auto (default) and ultra. Fixed prices are $0.012, $0.025, $0.10, $0.50 and $1.00; auto is metered ($0.10/ACU, $0.005/search) with a default $5 cap; ultra has a $20 cap.
Agent Ultra typically takes about 30 minutes and up to 3 hours; budget.maxDurationSeconds accepts 300 to 10,800 and applies only to ultra.
Agent run output has text, structured and grounding (per-field citations with confidence); stopReason is one of schema_satisfied, budget_reached, time_limit_reached, stopped, error, cancelled.
The Websets API requires a paid Websets plan with credits separate from Search API credits; the Free plan caps a webset at 25 verified results; the docs route new list-building work to Exa Agent.
Monitors need a webhook URL that is HTTPS and not localhost or a private IP; the minimum interval is 1 hour; POST /monitors/{id}/trigger runs one immediately; webhookSecret is returned only once.
The Batch API is Enterprise-only, in beta, and needs the header 'Exa-Beta: batches-2026-06-06'; items can target /search or /agent/runs.
Zero Data Retention is available for Search, Contents and Agent, but not for Answer or Websets; it is Enterprise-only and enabled per team.
Exa states it is SOC 2 Type II certified, with reports and a DPA at trust.exa.ai; HIPAA mode (compliance: 'hipaa') works on /search and /contents only, with instant or fast and cache-only retrieval.
Current package versions: exa-py 2.22.2 (Python 3.9 or later), exa-js 2.23.0, exa-mcp-server 3.4.1, @exalabs/ai-sdk 2.1.0.

The hosted MCP server is https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp with tools web_search_exa, web_fetch_exa, web_search_advanced_exa (opt-in) and agent_run (needs OAuth or an API key); the keyless tier is 3 QPS and 150 calls per day.

exa-py get_contents() adds text with 10,000 characters whenever no text, summary or extras is passed, even when highlights are requested; search() defaults to text with 10,000 characters unless contents=False.
exa-py agent.runs.create_and_wait times out after 120,000 ms by default and poll_until_finished after 3,600,000 ms; poll_interval is in milliseconds.
The OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions (model 'exa') routes to /answer, and /responses (model 'exa-agent') routes to Agent; high, xhigh and ultra effort in synchronous mode return a 400.
As of August 2026, Exa's index tracks 1.4 trillion URLs and serves 100 billion pages.

The enterprise page claims SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA with BAA, ZDR, contractual SLAs, custom indexing and forward-deployed engineers, and names customers including monday.com, HubSpot, Cognition, CodeRabbit, OpenRouter and 11x.

uncertainties: No authenticated calls were made (no API key; no account created). Unauthenticated /search returns an x402 payment challenge before any validation runs, so no field behavior was tested live.

Whether the API still accepts the legacy type values 'neural', 'keyword' or 'hybrid' is unknown: the spec enum omits them, but exa-py still lists 'neural' and exa-js lists 'keyword', 'neural' and 'hybrid'.

Exa's own latency figures disagree: docs say instant ~250 ms and auto ~1 s; the product page says Instant 323 ms and Auto ~1.2 s; the enterprise page says Instant P50 178 ms; the Feb 2026 changelog says sub-150 ms. Deep is 4-15 s in the docs and 4-12 s on the product page.
Runtime for fixed-effort Agent runs (minimal to xhigh) is not documented anywhere I read; only Ultra (~30 min typical, up to 3 h) and 'seconds to minutes' are stated.
Websets credit prices and plan tiers are not public; the docs point to https://websets.exa.ai/billing (logged-in) and the pricing page's websets tab showed no Websets content.
highlightScores: the April 2026 changelog says it was removed on May 1, 2026, but the current spec still lists it on results.

numResults cap for non-enterprise: docs say up to 100, but the Enterprise card lists 'requests above 25 results' as an enterprise feature and a NUM_RESULTS_EXCEEDED tag exists; the practical free or pay-as-you-go cap may be lower than 100.
additionalQueries limit: the spec says up to 10, the exa-py docstring says max 5.
Whether includeDomains and excludeDomains can be combined: an exa-py comment calls them exclusive; the spec does not say.
The exa-py comment that date filters exclude pages with no detected date was not confirmed in the API docs.
exa-js getContents() with no options sends no content fields; what the API returns by default in that case is not documented.
Baselayer price range differs between the pricing page ($0.15-$4.00 per order) and the Connect overview ($0.10-$4.00).
trust.exa.ai did not render any content, so the SOC 2 Type II claim rests on Exa's docs and enterprise page, not the reports themselves.
The exa.ai/demos page and customer case studies were not reviewed in this pass (outside this topic).

missing: Search already includes page contents at no extra charge for up to 10 results; after that it is $1 per 1,000 pages. So for the demo, one /search call with contents is cheaper than /search followed by /contents (source: https://exa.ai/docs/contents/quickstart.md line 17). Claim 14 lists only the standalone /contents price.

Double-billing trap, my inference from two sources: exa-py get_contents(urls, highlights=True) also adds 10,000-character text, and /contents bills each content type separately (pricing glossary: one page with text and highlights counts as two). Pass text=False when you only want highlights (sources: exa_py/api.py and https://exa.ai/docs/admin/pricing.md).

The product-page benchmark comes from the 'MultiLoko' dataset, the tab selected by default. On that tab Exa Fast (69.6%) scores higher than Auto (67.8%). Other rows: Parallel Adv 46.0%/2.7s, Parallel Basic 41.0%/1.3s. In a pitch, name the benchmark and do not say 80% vs 50% in general (https://exa.ai/products/search).

The enterprise page has its own Instant chart: Exa Instant 45%/178 ms, Parallel 37%/3051 ms, Brave 20%/559 ms, Tavily Ultra-Fast 11%/260 ms. The dataset is not named. The page also claims 'over 500,000 developers' and 'up to 94% fewer tokens'. Its logo strip also shows Cursor, Databricks, Klarna, Groq and AWS (https://exa.ai/enterprise).

Names and titles behind the enterprise-page quotes (useful for the pitch): Daniel Lereya, Chief Product and Technology Officer, monday.com; Praty Sharma, AI Lead, HubSpot; Walden Yan, Co-founder, Cognition; David Loker, VP of AI, CodeRabbit; Alex Atallah, CEO, OpenRouter; Prabhav Jain, CEO, 11x (https://exa.ai/enterprise).

How Exa describes the forward-deployed engineer (FDE) role on the enterprise page, relevant to AJ's interview: 'Work directly with Exa engineers on integration, evals, and retrieval quality' (https://exa.ai/enterprise).

Category changes from July 23, 2026: 'publication' replaced 'research paper', and the pdf, github and tweet categories are being deprecated. Older demos and tutorials may use the stale names (https://exa.ai/docs/changelog.md).

Exa Snapshot: the snapshotAsOf parameter returns the stored version of a page as of a chosen date, so a historical request never uses content from after that date. This fits a finance or market use case (https://exa.ai/docs/exa-spec.yaml; guide at https://exa.ai/docs/search/snapshot.md, listed in llms.txt but not opened by me).

Deprecated highlight parameters: numSentences and highlightsPerUrl (February 2, 2026 changelog). maxCharacters is now the way to control highlight length; highlights.md recommends plain highlights: true by default.
Agent run limits: each POST /agent/runs counts as two requests against QPS, and GET polling does not count against QPS (https://exa.ai/docs/admin/billing.md).
In the outputSchema quick-reference, the docs recommend Deep types by default and warn against choosing Deep only because the output is JSON (https://exa.ai/docs/search/best-practices.md).
Latency inconsistency not in the report: an older changelog entry gives deep-reasoning as 12-50 s and deep as 4-12 s, while the current docs say 12-40 s and 4-15 s (https://exa.ai/docs/changelog.md).
Claims 18, 19, 20 and 22 (Agent Ultra timing, stopReason values, Websets plan limits, Batch API beta header) were not re-verified in this pass.
https://exa.ai/blog/private-equity-case-study returned 404 when fetched, so do not cite it. The exa.ai/demos page and the customer case studies are still unreviewed, as the researcher noted.
